claim: The live routing concordance itself (~/.agents/skills/, 47 symlinks) resolves to the stale ~/.codex snapshot fleet instead of Sylveste/interverse — including a still-invocable deprecated flux-research skill — so agents read apocryphal copies regardless of canonical maintenance.

The ~/.codex snapshot fleet converges perfectly toward the wrong exemplar: plugin_repo_url hardcodes github.com/mistakeknot and ensure_repo fast-forwards, so all 39 clones report behind=0 vs origin while 20 of 37 lag their Sylveste source versions (interwatch 0.3.3 vs 0.6.1) — and ~/.agents/skills routes every agent harness into these GitHub-frozen snapshots instead of the living checkouts AGENTS.md declares canonical.

META-FINDING — implemented-never-wired: four fully implemented and tested intercore subsystems (lifecycle stall detector f-133, scheduler engine + crash recovery f-136, audit chain f-143, plus replay reexecution f-134) have zero production callers — each merged without the CLI wiring commit. The pattern extends beyond intercore (compact guard unwired f-128, inert-config lever f-107, dead gate-audit emitter f-101): this is a landing-process gap, not four independent oversights. Highest-leverage single fix: one `ic sweep`/`ic doctor --fix` command wiring dispatch.Poll-based reaping + lifecycle CheckStalls, converting all silent wedges into observable, contract-visible state.

Replay certifies the curve with holes: `ic run replay` gates only on run.Status==completed, builds the timeline from whatever events exist, and exits 0 in simulate mode — no completeness check against the dispatches table, no events_expected vs events_found, exit code carries no sparsity signal. A run executed through the 15 nil-recorder paths replays 'successfully' with only phase events; reconstruct.go:36 also silently drops coordination/review/discovery sources, so even recorded coordination events are invisible to certification. The certification instrument converts a known instrumentation gap into a false certificate that recovery and reexecute gating will trust. (Verifier V1: genuine emergent, upheld.)

The filesystem lock has a 5-second staleness fuse: tryBreakStale breaks any lock purely by owner.json age with no heartbeat or PID-liveness check, so mutual exclusion does not exist for any dispatch longer than 5 seconds.

The demarch->sylveste colophon rename orphaned 37 byte-identical gitleaks-waiver validators: is_managed_file greps only the new marker, so all 37 classify as 'existing unmanaged file' and are SKIPped forever — both lineages claim v1, and every future template change propagates to only 10/47 of the fleet.

emitInterspectEvent — the only audit emitter on the Go gate path — calls `ic events add`, a subcommand that does NOT exist (events.go:18 accepts only tail/cursor/emit/record/list-review/list-agency); rc=3 is discarded by `_, _ =`, so the calibration_skip_gate 'audit event' advertised at phase.go:343-348 has never landed anywhere (V1: events-add-void upheld). Working vehicle is `ic events record --source=interspect`.

The lib-intercore.sh twin guard is DOUBLE-BLIND: both copies stamp INTERCORE_WRAPPER_VERSION 1.1.0 over 266 diff lines; the only sync check points at ../../hub/clavain/hooks/lib-intercore.sh — dead since the hub/clavain->os/Clavain move — and even if repointed compares only the identical version string. All 9 runtime hooks execute the Clavain copy while the core copy is the nominal 'source' (executed/edited inverted), and the twins diverge in OPPOSITE directions per function (sentinels fail open in Clavain, temp-file fallback in core; state ops propagate errors in Clavain, swallow in core) — wholesale canonizing either copy flips failure direction for one function class across all 9 hooks (V2: genuine-emergent, upheld).

Audit chain wired naively manufactures false tamper verdicts: New() snapshots lastHash/sequenceNum into memory (audit.go:81-127); two CLI processes producing transitions for the same run both read prev_hash=H and both write sequence n+1 — a chain fork that VerifyIntegrity reports as 'sequence gap'/'hash chain broken' on an honest firing. Spurious alarms retrain operators to ignore the verifier; real tampering later gets dismissed as 'the fork bug again' — the witness devalues the entire record's authority. Emergent trust-erosion path neither parent produces alone.

ic events tail --consumer advances the cursor on stdout write before the consumer processes, so a crash between read and insert silently drops the whole batch, with the at-most-once window and 24h cursor TTL in no contract doc and no ack/replay path.

upstreams.json is a palimpsest: 39 of 65 fileMap targets point at paths extracted to companion plugins long ago, so running sync-upstreams.sh would re-materialize deleted folios over the living corpus.
Every ic dispatch subcommand constructs the store with a nil event recorder, so spawn/poll/wait/kill transitions leave no row in dispatch_events unless auto-spawned by ic run advance.

f-048 PARTIAL with corrected mechanism: commands/degraded-modes.yaml is advisory-only (no code reads it); the code-enforced lever is project-level .clavain/agency-spec.yaml — gate_mode:off returns 0 with NO log line, shadow always passes, the Go enforce-gate defaults to shadow on any spec-load error, and no audit event is emitted anywhere on the path, contradicting the 'admin-controlled, same trust as Makefiles' comment.

Upstream deletions never propagate and the sync pointer advances over the deletion event: status==D files are silently skipped, then lastSyncedCommit advances unconditionally, so local copies of texts deleted upstream persist forever, still mapped in upstreams.json, certified as converged by a catalog whose ancestor pointer has moved past their death.

Adjudication of f-029 x f-014: f-029 substantiated — 44 of 47 ~/.agents/skills symlinks resolve to ~/.codex snapshot clones with uneven freshness (non-default-profile clones frozen at 2026-03-24); f-014's 'covered install cache' frame is correct about design intent but holds only for the clavain clone.

tryBreakStale breaks any lock older than 5s purely by owner.json created timestamp; pidAlive exists one file over but is wired only into Clean, never the acquire/break path — mutual exclusion void for any holder >5s, and TestStaleBreaking actively pins the bad behavior as correct.
Drift detection covers interverse companions only as git clones under ~/.codex and only in --full mode; marketplace-cache installs of ~58 plugins and all Kimi-host installs have no freshness check.

codex-auto-refresh.sh is dead automation: no crontab entry, no LaunchAgent, refresh log never written — the only mechanism that would pull all companion clones has never run on this machine, while docs imply freshness. Dead automation is worse than none.

zklw (first probe) replicates the snapshot-routing pattern — 46 ~/.agents/skills links resolve to ~/.codex/<plugin> snapshots (interlock stale since 2026-07-04) — with a wrinkle: ~/.codex/clavain does not exist and the clavain skill points to a standalone ~/projects/Clavain GitHub clone, a THIRD undeclared Clavain lineage alongside Sylveste/os/Clavain and ~/.codex/clavain; no crontab/systemd timer runs codex-auto-refresh there either.

The correct contract is ALREADY WRITTEN in intercore-vision.md:336-349 — read-only tail, explicit `ic events cursor set` after processing, durable vs ephemeral cursors, prune with durable-cursor protection, stable per-source ids — and never implemented (cursor subcommands are list/reset/register only; tail auto-advances; prune absent; TTL 24h not 7d). The fix is converge-code-to-vision; no new design needed (V4: contract-written-not-implemented upheld).

SKILL-compact.md is the executed contract while SKILL.md is the edited source: the compact directive (in 10 Clavain SKILL.md files) instructs agents to load the compact unconditionally; 13/15 pairs have SKILL.md newer (up to 126 days), the hash guard confirms 10 stale compacts, 6 pairs lack manifests entirely. The root guard's registry is stale AND contradicts a canonization decision: it tests interflux/flux-drive whose compact was DELIBERATELY deleted in the B4 canonization (sylveste-s46z — compact had silently dropped Phase 2.5 orchestration), plus phantom entries interserve/brainstorming — the consolidation guard demands re-creation of a file consolidation deliberately killed.

The flux-drive→flux-engine rename commit interflux@18d393e silently re-created a 310-line SKILL-compact.md — directly contradicting d2a1ded's deliberate canonization to a single SKILL.md (motivated by the compact silently dropping Phase 2.5 reaction-round orchestration). The re-created compact has no compact-mode preamble in SKILL.md and is itself stale per the checker. Canonization was half-executed, then partially reverted by accident. Verifier V6: upheld.

Catalog staleness disk-verified: 39 of 65 fileMap targets do not exist locally — and several were not deleted but RELOCATED (systematic-debugging/test-driven-development/verification-before-completion now live under interverse/intertest/skills/, oracle refs under the standalone interpeer repo) while upstreams.json still claims Clavain paths as their sync targets. Relocation changes the fix: repoint to the new owner's sync config, not just delete. (f-028 residual, upheld in full.)

All 15/15 Clavain SKILL.md/SKILL-compact.md pairs now fail the guard's own freshness check (round-2 measured 13/15): 9 genuine source-hash drifts + 6 pairs missing .skill-compact-manifest.json entirely; oldest drift 126 days. All 4 non-Clavain registry entries with existing dirs also fail — the compact fleet is 0% fresh, and agents load the stale compact unconditionally per the compact directive.

The compact-drift guard is wired nowhere: no root CI workflow mentions compact, none of Clavain's 7 workflows invoke it, and the pre-commit hook doesn't either. Broken guard + zero enforcement = compacts drift silently — f-008's effect-claim confirmed at fleet scale.
A working compact-drift guard hook exists only in interflux; Clavain's 15 SKILL/SKILL-compact pairs have no equivalent, which is how the landing-a-change drift went unnoticed.

Split-brain routing with no documented rule: clavain/alwe/zaka links point at canonical Sylveste working trees while 44 siblings point at ~/.codex snapshots — two freshness semantics in one directory, and an agent cannot tell which regime it is reading.

install.sh is the exception that adjudicates intent: find_local_clavain_source() prefers the local checkout and GitHub clones are curl-pipe fallbacks only — GitHub-as-exemplar is INTENTIONAL as a distribution channel for machines without the tree, ACCIDENTAL as the standing default on machines that have it.
The CLAVAIN_SKIP_GATE block message advertises '(audited)' but no audit record is written on either path — a user-facing audit overclaim printed exactly when the gate is being bypassed.

interflux's per-plugin drift hook — the guard f-008 credited as the only working one — was deliberately deleted in canonization commit d2a1ded, then resurrected onto main via b5f537c ('rescue uncommitted deliverables') but never registered in hooks/hooks.json, so it is an inert dead file. f-008's premise is stale on both sides.

deletedLocally is a reader-with-no-writer channel: wired into both engines (bash DELETED: guard at sync-upstreams.sh:124; Python SKIP_DELETED at classify.py:58) but the array is empty and grep for any writer returns nothing — negative events have a consumer and no producer. (f-090 re-verified verbatim; V4 upheld.)

The resurrection guard is presence-based, not intent-based: SKIP:not-present-locally fires only because the file is absent. If any of the 39 stale paths is recreated for an unrelated reason, the next weekly sync re-engages the mapping and AUTO-overwrites the file with upstream content via automated PR. Latent, not live — the f-028 hazard demoted from 'impossible' to 'incidentally prevented'.
A finished interlab campaign report and 8 harness scripts sit unlinked at the Clavain repository root, and interlab.md's results table cites doctor.md — renamed clavain-doctor.md since.

Version-stamp schizophrenia in the twin library: header comment says 'Version: 0.1.0 (source: infra/intercore/lib-intercore.sh)' — a provenance path that no longer exists — while the machine stamp says 1.1.0, historical docs cite v0.4.0/v0.6.0, AGENTS.md claims '44 functions' and cli-reference.md '45 functions' against twin surfaces that actually differ (Clavain copy adds 5 run_* wrappers) — three version witnesses plus two surface-size witnesses, so no consumer can tell which string IS the contract version, and any canonization that bumps only one witness re-creates the ambiguity that hid the 1.1.0/266-diff-lines split.

RECOMMENDATION (analytical): prune + shrink migration in 3 steps — (1) prune the 39 dead fileMap entries (repoint relocated skills to their interverse owners' sync configs, demote true deletions into deletedLocally so the guard becomes intent-based); (2) teach clavain_sync a shrink rule (N=3 consecutive SKIP -> deletedLocally; upstream deletion -> local deletion proposal in the sync PR); (3) switch sync.yml to `python3 -m clavain_sync` and delete the bash engine after one clean cycle. Side observation: ~39 fossil SKIP lines/run desensitize weekly-PR reviewers to the SKIP category that also carries protected/deleted signals.

The catalog's deletion registry is vestigial: syncConfig.deletedLocally is empty and no lifecycle step (sync engines, CI, install, doctor) ever writes to it, so the catalog is append-only — and the f-028 resurrection scenario is prevented only by the incidental SKIP:not-present-locally guard, not by any recorded intent.

plugin_repo_url() hardcodes https://github.com/mistakeknot/%s.git and ensure_repo() clones/ff-pulls every companion from GitHub; there is NO code path that prefers the local Sylveste/interverse/<plugin> checkouts (71 present, each a live git repo) — the canonical tree is invisible to the installer (direct re-confirmation of f-084 core).
